paper_metadata.title: Simulation of a Variational Quantum Perceptron using Grover’s Algorithm

experiments.description: Quantum variational perceptron (QVP) evaluated on the Iris dataset using a variational quantum circuit and classical optimization, with accuracy and loss tracked over iterations.

algorithm.ansatz: Parameterized unitary circuit with two-qubit parameterized gates and generic unitary gates plus CNOT gates
algorithm.convergence_criteria: trained over 100 iterations; no explicit stopping criterion reported

hyperparameters.loss_function: average over N samples: L(θ) = (1/N) Σ l(π(x_i;θ), y_i)
hyperparameters.gradient_method: analytic/parameter-shift-like circuit evaluation via modified parameters
hyperparameters.encoding_dimension: amplitude encoding with p qubits for state φ(x)|0^p⟩

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Classical data x are encoded into amplitudes of a quantum state; paper states a dataset of M inputs with N features needs n = log(N*M) qubits.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize L(θ) = (1/N) Σ_i l(π(x_i;θ), y_i), where π(x;θ) = P(q0 = 1 | x; θ)

problem_instance.description: Binary classification on the Iris dataset using a quantum perceptron model.

dataset_specification.description: No detailed preprocessing, feature selection, or train/validation split reported in the text.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Input values are rescaled to fit circuit angles; amplitude encoding is used.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Accuracy reported over iterations on training and validation sets; loss curve plotted over 100 iterations.

noise_model.noise_type: noise modeling supported by ibmq qasm simulator; specific noise parameters not reported

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical data are rescaled to fit rotation angles; amplitude encoding used.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measurement of q0 probability used to compute class probabilities and loss.

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: loss decreases over iterations and is reported to converge better than baselines; approximate final loss around 0.4 for QVP-G, not QVP

speedup_claims.conditions: Grover algorithm background; not specifically demonstrated for the perceptron benchmark
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper claims Grover amplitude amplification improves classification training/measurement, but no direct runtime complexity comparison is provided for the Iris experiment.

speedup_claims.factor: fewer iterations to reach high validation accuracy
speedup_claims.conditions: On the Iris dataset with 2-qubit QVP/QVP-G models over 100 iterations
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states the quantum models reach 99% validation accuracy in fewer iterations, but the table shows the classical perceptron also reaches high accuracy; no formal convergence criterion or runtime is reported.

experiments.description: Quantum variational perceptron with Grover amplification (QVP-G) evaluated on the Iris dataset, comparing accuracy and loss against QVP and classical perceptron baselines.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Variational Perceptron with Grover algorithm (QVP-G / QVPG)
algorithm.ansatz: Parameterized unitary circuit with Grover-style amplitude amplification appended; Hadamard, CNOT, controlled-Z, and Pauli-X gates
algorithm.convergence_criteria: trained over 100 iterations; no explicit stopping criterion reported

hyperparameters.loss_function: average over N samples: L(θ) = (1/N) Σ l(π(x_i;θ), y_i)
hyperparameters.input_rescaling: classical inputs rescaled to fit circuit angles

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Classical data x are encoded into amplitudes of a quantum state; the model uses two qubits and measures a particular qubit configuration for classification.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize L(θ) = (1/N) Σ_i l(π(x_i;θ), y_i), with Grover circuit used to amplify the target state's amplitude before measurement
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Grover diffusion/amplitude amplification used to increase probability of the target output state

problem_instance.description: Binary classification on the Iris dataset using a variational perceptron augmented with Grover search/amplitude amplification.

dataset_specification.description: No detailed preprocessing, feature selection, or train/validation split reported in the text.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Input values are rescaled to fit circuit angles; classification is obtained by counting occurrences of a measured qubit configuration.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Accuracy reported over iterations on training and validation sets; loss curve plotted over 100 iterations.

noise_model.noise_type: noise modeling supported by ibmq qasm simulator; specific noise parameters not reported

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical data are rescaled to fit rotation angles; amplitude encoding used.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measurement counts of a particular qubit configuration are used to infer class labels and compute loss/accuracy.

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: loss decreases over iterations and is reported to converge better than QVP and CP; approximate final loss around 0.4

speedup_claims.conditions: Grover algorithm background; amplitude amplification used in the classifier
speedup_claims.caveats: The quadratic speedup is a property of Grover search in general, not a measured speedup for the Iris classification task.

speedup_claims.factor: higher validation accuracy and faster convergence than QVP and CP
speedup_claims.baseline_method: quantum variational perceptron and classical perceptron
speedup_claims.conditions: Iris dataset, 2 qubits, 100 iterations, IBM ibmq_qasm_simulator
speedup_claims.caveats: No wall-clock time, shot count, or statistical uncertainty is reported; improvement is based on accuracy/loss curves and table values.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(sqrt(N)) for Grover search as described in background
